reviewed_by: Claude: Nebula-wide Butler check rotated hosts across every Act project
reason: Core change. A project worker reads only its own project, so every Act project's worker computed itself as the Nebula-wide check anchor and whichever tick first saw the shared clock due won (live: 10 hosts in 8 hours), flipping the check runtime, the shared '*' default runtime and the summary target, and letting a second check start beside a still-open one. ButlerGlobalState gains host_seen_at; a worker that cannot read the recorded host defers to it until it has been silent for three intervals, and the host refreshes host_seen_at once per interval while its check is open. Selected the Butler instructions suite (new scoped-worker rotation and full-read anchor tests), the home-host, global-check scope and check-summary suites that read the host fields.
exclusions: test_execution_locks.py global-check concurrency is PostgreSQL-only and not wired to CI Postgres; run locally against Postgres 16 (2 passed). No UI or migration change; full suites not run.
